NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>SOURCE 1 shows the street front; SOURCE 2–3 show opposite rear corners, SOURCE 4 the roof, and SOURCE 5–6 opposite front corners. Shared landmarks establish the brick main volume, dark vertically divided left facade, two recessed balconies, narrow stacked front glazing, raised glazed roof room, lower dark roof volume, and rear/side openings. CURRENT retains these principal elements, but changes the entrance enclosure, lower front glazing divisions, and upper rear brick relief. No dimensions are supplied; concealed construction and joint integrity cannot be verified from screenshots alone.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: CURRENT closes the central entrance with a broad continuous barred gate. The source photograph shows an open central approach with a narrower gate beside it; SOURCE 5–6 likewise retain an opening between the boundary-wall sections.
action: Locally revise the central gate width and placement to restore the source entrance opening and visible approach steps.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="front">problem: CURRENT adds a central vertical mullion through the two lower lights of the narrow right-hand window stack. These lower lights are undivided vertically in the photograph and SOURCE 6.
action: Remove the additional lower vertical mullion and align the horizontal frame divisions with the source, retaining the upper paired glazing.</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="rear">problem: SOURCE 2–4 show a distinct rectangular brick apron projecting below the upper-right rear roof edge, partly overlapping the window zone. CURRENT rear appears flush beneath the horizontal gutter, losing this relief.
action: Restore that local brick apron and its visible bottom and side edges; connect it cleanly to the roof return without covering more of the opening than shown.</issue>
<keep>Three upper rear windows arranged as one centered opening above a pair, with a second pair below.
Three vertically aligned small rectangular openings on the right side.
Three-column upper glazing in the raised roof room.
Thin dark coping along the front brick parapet.</keep>
